Public Portion 
 1. Review and Discussion of the Current Status of the Proposed Palmer Renewable 
Energy Biomass Power Plant, Including Pending Legal Proceedings, Environmental 
and Public Health Concerns, and Potential Impacts on the East Springfield 
Community. 
On October 27, 2026, the Public Safety and Health and Human Services Committees, chaired by 
Councilor Gerry Martin, met jointly to review the proposed Palmer Renewable Energy biomass 
power plant and related public health, environmental, and safety concerns. The committees 
reviewed the project's permitting history and litigation, including the reinstatement of previously 
issued building permits following an Appeals Court decision. Additional state and federal
environmental approvals remain outstanding, and the potential requirement for a new special 
permit under the City's zoning ordinance remains disputed. Discussion addressed air quality, 
respiratory health, environmental justice, anticipated truck traffic, and the potential impact of 
additional industrial emissions. Members also reviewed changes to state energy policies and 
financial incentives affecting the project's viability. 
 
The committees discussed upcoming proceedings identified for November 9 and December 8, 
2026, including matters related to state air quality permitting. Attorney Ken Shea agreed to 
clarify the nature of the proceedings and the City's involvement. Proposed legislation addressing 
biomass energy classifications and subsidies was reviewed, including Senate Bills S.2136 and 
S.2137 and House Bills H.3210 and H.3211. Discussion included potential legislative support, 
public testimony, and available municipal legal and regulatory options. 
 
Councilor Michael Fenton recommended considering a Committee of the Whole meeting in 
executive session to discuss potential litigation strategies, subject to applicable legal 
requirements. He cautioned against adopting a resolution opposing the project before any 
potential special permit proceedings to preserve the Council's impartiality. Councilor Brian 
Santaniello supported further consideration of legal and legislative options. Councilor Martin 
indicated that a follow-up meeting would be coordinated in the coming weeks. No formal 
recommendation or substantive vote was recorded. A motion to adjourn was made and seconded, 
and the meeting adjourned at 1:40 p.m.
